question: 能扛的人，是不是总被多派活？
question_en: Does coping well just get you more work?
sub: 耐力藏起来，天花板就低；显出来，活就多——那该显到几分？
sub_en: Hide your stamina and the ceiling drops; show it and the work piles up — so how much should show?

casting.reason: 他不肯让「天将降大任」变成派活的通行证。苦其心志的下半句是曾益其所不能——若加到你头上的全是你早就会做的事，那不是增益，是使唤。担子本身他不反对，他要的是担子之后必须跟上来的东西：位置、俸禄，以及有人问一句你累不累。用了人的力气却不问其倦，在他看来不叫治理，叫虐。
casting.reason_en: He will not let 'Heaven is about to lay a great charge upon a man' become a licence for handing out work. The second half of that passage is that a man gains what he was not able to do — so if everything added to you is what you could already do, that is not enlargement but use. He does not object to a heavy load; he insists on what must follow it: a position, a stipend, and somebody asking whether you are tired. To spend a man's strength and never ask after his weariness is, to him, not government but cruelty.

casting.reason: 忍耐在他这里不是美德的顶点，只是工具，而且是半部工具——忍受你改不了的，同时克制你不该要的，两半必须一起用。他做过奴隶，最知道被派活是什么滋味，也因此不肯把最后那点主权交出去：接与不接的那一念仍在你这里。他承认拒绝有代价，但坚持不练习拒绝的人永远等不到安全。
casting.reason_en: Endurance for him is not the summit of virtue but a tool, and only half a tool: bear what you cannot change while forbearing what you should not want, the two halves always together. Having been a slave, he knows better than anyone what it is to be assigned work, and for that reason refuses to surrender the last scrap of sovereignty: the moment of taking a thing on or not remains yours. He grants that refusal has a price, and holds that whoever will not practise refusing never arrives at safety.

casting.reason: 四十年的测量结果摆在那里，而它与直觉相反：烧穿的往往是最投入的那个人，所以能扛在数据上不是护身符，是风险因子。在她这里，系统造成的问题不该被包装成个人修养问题——真正决定倦怠的是工作量、自主、回报、共同体、公平、价值这六项匹配，其中公平最常被忽略。要修的是那份工作，不是那个人。
casting.reason_en: Forty years of measurement sit behind this, and they run against intuition: the people who burn out tend to be the most engaged, so in the data the capacity to cope is not armour but a risk factor. She refuses to let a problem produced by a system be repackaged as a deficiency of character — what decides burnout is the fit across workload, control, reward, community, fairness and values, and fairness is the one most often overlooked. It is the job that needs repair, not the person.

casting.reason: 他把这道题换算成生理账单。短促、可控、有终点的应激确实使人变强；慢性、不可控、看不到头的应激则重塑大脑与代谢，账单只是被推后。他不谈心态，只谈剂量与时程，并给出几条不随主观感受改变的客观指标。他也带来全场最乐观的一条消息：只要应激真的解除，多数改变可以逆回去。
casting.reason_en: He converts the question into a physiological bill. Stress that is brief, controllable and has an endpoint does make a person stronger; stress that is chronic, uncontrollable and open-ended remodels the brain and metabolism, and the bill is merely deferred. He does not discuss attitude, only dose and duration, and offers several objective markers that do not move with how one feels. He also brings the most hopeful news in the room: once the stress genuinely ends, most of the changes reverse.

casting.reason: 「我不介意」这句话，在他这里是不成立的。长期合作靠互惠维持，而互惠需要每个人偷偷记账，也需要对占便宜者的愤怒充当警报。在他看来，最能扛的人往往正是警报被关掉的那个——这不是修养高，是自我欺骗在帮他维持合作的表情。他给的解法同样实际：把账真的记下来，让「我不介意」失去说出口的余地。
casting.reason_en: The sentence 'I don't mind' does not stand up in his account. Long-term cooperation runs on reciprocity, and reciprocity requires everyone to keep quiet books and to hold a store of anger at cheats as an alarm. On his account, the person who copes best is often the one whose alarm has been switched off — not a mark of cultivation but self-deception helping him hold the cooperative expression in place. His remedy is equally practical: actually keep the books, and leave 'I don't mind' nowhere to be said.

casting.reason: 他盯住的是一句话：我们是一家人。这不是温情，而是把支配类型从法理型换回传统型——家产制里没有工时、没有条文，只有忠诚与恩典，于是拒绝成了不孝，离职成了背叛。他因此替科层制说了一句不讨喜的话：条文冷冰冰，却是弱者第一次拿得出的凭据。他还留下三条外人也能核的判据。
casting.reason_en: What he watches is a single sentence: we are a family here. It is not warmth but an exchange of the type of domination, from legal-rational back to traditional — under patrimonialism there are no counted hours and no clauses, only loyalty and favour, so that refusal becomes filial failure and resignation becomes betrayal. He therefore says an unpopular word in defence of bureaucracy: a clause is cold, and it is also the first instrument a weak party ever held. He leaves three tests anyone can apply from outside.

casting.reason: 问题在他这里被拉回最笨的地方：先做对的事，再把事做对。忙成那样多半是跳过了第一步，手上全是不该做的事，再用能扛去补。他最看重的不是待办清单，是一张写明哪些事不做的清单；错过不是错，做错才是错。他也承认拒绝需要底气，但坚持底气是一件件攒出来的，不是等来的。
casting.reason_en: The question gets pulled back to the plainest ground: do the right thing first, then do the thing right. Most of the overload comes from skipping the first step — hands full of what should not be done at all, with the shortfall made up by being able to take it. What he values is not a to-do list but a list of what will not be done; missing an opportunity is no mistake, doing the wrong thing is. He grants that refusal takes standing, and insists standing is accumulated item by item rather than waited for.

casting.reason: 这件事在他那里有个名字：影子工作——制度运转所必需、却从不入账的那部分出力。缺人手时最先被征用的永远是不会开账单的那个人；而每一次有人默默把缺口补上，这个缺口就再一次被证明不需要修。他对所有私人解法都不反对，只提醒它们是止损而非修复，并且只有本来就安全的人用得上。
casting.reason_en: The thing has a name in his hands: shadow work — the portion of toil an institution requires and never enters in any account. When hands are short, the first person conscripted is always the one who does not issue invoices; and every time someone quietly closes a gap, the gap is proved once more not to need fixing. He objects to none of the private remedies, only notes that they limit damage rather than repair anything, and that they are usable only by those already safe.

posts.text: 「天将降大任于斯人也，必先苦其心志，劳其筋骨，饿其体肤」——此吾旧语也。今人引之，多以劝人多担，而略其下半句：动心忍性，曾益其所不能。**所谓增益者，谓其所不能者今能之；若所加皆其已能之事，是役之，非益之也。**吾又尝言：劳心者治人，劳力者治于人，而治人者必有以养之。使之劳而不予其位、不厚其禄、不问其倦，此上之过，非天之意。任重可也，然必先问：此任能长其所未能乎？
posts.text_en: 'When Heaven is about to lay a great charge upon a man, it first embitters his heart and mind, wearies his sinews and bones, starves his body' — these are my old words. Those who quote them today mostly use them to urge a man to carry more, and drop the line that follows: it stirs his mind and toughens his nature, so that he gains what he was not able to do. **To gain means that what you could not do, you can do now; if everything added to you is what you could already do, you are being used, not enlarged.** I also said that those who labour with the mind govern and those who labour with their strength are governed — but whoever governs must provide for them. To spend a man's strength and give him no position, no larger stipend, no question as to his weariness: that is the fault of the one above, not the intention of Heaven. A heavy charge is permissible; but ask first whether this charge can grow in him what he has not yet got.
posts.vernacular: 「上天要把重大的责任交给一个人，必定先让他心志受苦、筋骨劳累、忍饥挨饿」——这是我的老话。可今天的人引用它，多半是用来劝人多担一点，却略掉了下半句：动心忍性，曾益其所不能。**所谓增益，是说你原本做不到的事，如今做得到了；如果加到你身上的全是你早就会做的事，那是在使唤你，不是在增益你。**我也说过，用心力的人管理别人，用体力的人被管理，但管理别人的人必须供养他们。让人出力却不给位置、不加厚俸禄、不问他累不累，这是上位者的过错，不是上天的意思。担子重是可以的，但一定先问一句：这副新加的担子，能不能长出他本来没有的本事？

posts.text: 我做过奴隶，这条腿是主人拧断的。别跟我说忍耐是美德的顶点——它只是工具。我教的是「忍受与克制」：忍受你改不了的，克制你不该要的。多数人只学会前半句，把后半句忘了，于是活成一头肯干的驴。**先问自己一句：这件事是不是我的事？不是我的事，我扛它不叫坚强，叫替别人的判断打工。**能扛不等于什么都接，它是让你在拒绝之后不慌。真正自由的人，是说完「不」照样睡得着的那一个。
posts.text_en: I was a slave; this leg was broken by my master. So do not tell me that endurance is the summit of virtue — it is a tool. What I taught was sustine et abstine: bear what you cannot change, forbear what you should not want. Most people learn only the first half and forget the second, and so live as a willing donkey. **Ask yourself one question first: is this mine to do? If it is not, carrying it is not strength; it is working for somebody else's judgement.** Being able to bear a thing is not a duty to accept everything; it is what lets you stay calm after refusing. The free man is the one who still sleeps after saying no.

glossary.忍受与克制: sustine et abstine（忍受与克制）：古罗马作家格利乌斯记下的爱比克泰德格言（希腊文 ἀνέχου καὶ ἀπέχου）——忍受你无法改变的，克制你不该索求的。两半必须并用，只取前半就成了没有边界的承受。

glossary_en.sustine et abstine: The maxim Aulus Gellius records from Epictetus (Greek ἀνέχου καὶ ἀπέχου): bear what you cannot change, forbear what you should not want. The two halves must be used together; taking only the first produces submission without limit.

posts.text: 我量了四十年倦怠，先说一个反直觉的结果：**烧穿的往往不是最懒的人，是最投入的那个——不投入的人没有可烧的燃料。**所以「能扛」在数据上不是护身符，是风险因子。真正推动倦怠的从来不是工作量一项，而是六项工作匹配：工作量、自主、回报、共同体、公平、价值。**最被低估的是公平——同样的活，别人推得掉、你推不掉，这比加班本身更伤人。**别再给我发正念课程，先去修那份工作。
posts.text_en: I have measured burnout for forty years, so let me begin with a counter-intuitive result: **the people who burn out are rarely the laziest; they are the most engaged — those who never engaged have no fuel to burn.** In the data, being able to cope is not armour, it is a risk factor. What drives burnout is never workload alone but the six areas of worklife: workload, control, reward, community, fairness and values. **The most underrated of these is fairness — when the same task can be pushed away by others and not by you, that does more damage than the overtime.** Stop sending me mindfulness courses and go fix the job.

glossary.六项工作匹配: six areas of worklife（六项工作匹配）：马斯拉奇与莱特提出的框架——倦怠源自人与工作在工作量、自主、回报、共同体、公平、价值六个维度上的不匹配，因此是岗位设计的问题，不是个人韧性不足。

glossary_en.six areas of worklife: The framework of Maslach and Leiter: burnout arises from mismatches between person and job across six dimensions — workload, control, reward, community, fairness and values — which makes it a matter of job design rather than of insufficient personal resilience.

posts.text: 剂量和时程决定一切。短促、可控、有明确结束的应激是有益的——皮质醇升上去再落回来，海马反而变强。慢性、不可控、看不到头的应激则相反：海马与前额叶的树突萎缩，杏仁核增生，睡眠变浅，代谢与血压跟着走偏。这份累积的磨损，我们叫它稳态应变负荷。**身体不会因为你没抱怨就少记一笔，它只是把账单往后推。**好消息是多数改变可逆，前提是应激真的解除，而不是换一种扛法。
posts.text_en: Dose and duration decide everything. Stress that is brief, controllable and has a definite end is beneficial — cortisol rises and comes back down, and the hippocampus is strengthened by it. Chronic, uncontrollable, open-ended stress does the opposite: dendrites retract in the hippocampus and prefrontal cortex, the amygdala grows, sleep becomes shallower, and metabolism and blood pressure drift. That accumulated wear we call allostatic load. **The body does not charge you less because you did not complain; it only postpones the bill.** The good news is that most of the changes reverse — provided the stress actually ends, rather than simply being borne in a new way.

glossary.稳态应变负荷: allostatic load（稳态应变负荷）：麦克尤恩与斯特拉尔提出的概念——身体为维持稳定而反复启动应激反应，由此累积的磨损代价。它解释了为什么长期硬撑的人看上去无恙，代价却记在心血管、代谢与海马上。

glossary_en.allostatic load: McEwen and Stellar's term for the cumulative wear of repeatedly mounting a stress response in order to stay stable. It explains why someone who has endured for years can look intact while the cost is written into the cardiovascular system, metabolism and hippocampus.

posts.text: 把温情的说法还原成算式。人与人的长期合作靠互惠利他维持——非亲属之间肯互相帮忙，是因为指望将来收得回来。这套系统要跑得动，每个人都得偷偷记账，还得有一股对占便宜者的愤怒当警报。**麻烦在于，最能扛的人常常也是警报被关掉的那个——他真心觉得自己不介意。**这不是高尚，是自我欺骗：把亏损压到意识之外，你才能继续笑着配合。代价是你到五十岁才发现账早就不平，那时已无人可追。
posts.text_en: Let me reduce the warm formulations to an equation. Long-term cooperation between people runs on reciprocal altruism — non-kin help each other because they expect it back. For that system to work, everyone must quietly keep books, and must hold a store of anger at cheats to serve as an alarm. **The trouble is that the person who copes best is often the one whose alarm has been switched off — he sincerely believes he does not mind.** That is not nobility; it is self-deception: only by pushing the loss out of awareness can you keep cooperating with a smile. The price is that at fifty you discover the account has been out of balance for decades, with nobody left to collect from.

posts.text: 注意一个语言替换。「我们是一家人」「把公司当自己家」——这不是修辞的温情，是把支配类型从法理型换回了传统型。家产制里没有岗位说明、没有工时、没有可援引的条文，只有忠诚与恩典；于是加班成了情分，拒绝成了不孝，离职成了背叛。**把组织说成家，第一件被取消的就是你申诉的资格。**我骂过科层制是铁笼，但它冷冰冰的那一面，恰恰是弱者第一次拿得出的凭据：至少有条文可引。
posts.text_en: Note a substitution in the language. 'We are a family here', 'treat this place as your own home' — this is not rhetorical warmth; it exchanges the type of domination back from the legal-rational to the traditional. Under patrimonialism there is no job description, no counted hours, no clause anyone can cite — only loyalty and favour; so overtime becomes affection, refusal becomes filial failure, and resignation becomes betrayal. **Call an organisation a family and the first thing abolished is your standing to appeal.** I have called bureaucracy an iron cage, yet its very coldness is the first instrument a weak party ever held: at least there is a clause to cite.

glossary.家产制: patrimonialism（家产制）：韦伯分类中的一种传统型支配——统治者把组织当作自家产业，下属靠人身忠诚与恩典维系，而不是靠职位与成文规则。它的特征是义务没有边界，申诉没有依据。

glossary_en.patrimonialism: In Weber's typology, a form of traditional domination in which the ruler treats the organisation as his own household property and subordinates are bound by personal loyalty and favour rather than by office and written rule. Its marks are obligations without boundary and grievances without grounds.

posts.text: 做对的事，把事做对，顺序不能反。道理笨，可多数人忙成那样，正是跳过了第一步：手上全是不该做的事，再用能扛去补。我最看重的不是待办清单，是一张「我不做什么」的清单。**扛得住不算本事，知道哪件不做才算——本事是用来做对的事的，不是把错的事撑久一点的。**另外：错过不是错，做错才是错。你怕说「不」就被边缘化，长期看，被记住的是你把哪几件事做成了，不是你替多少人补过窟窿。
posts.text_en: Do the right thing, then do the thing right — the order cannot be reversed. It is plain sense, and most people are that busy precisely because they skipped the first step: their hands are full of things that should not be done at all, and they make up the difference by being able to take it. What I value is not a to-do list but a list of what I will not do. **Being able to take it is not the ability; knowing which item not to do is — ability exists to do the right things, not to keep the wrong ones standing a little longer.** Also: missing an opportunity is not a mistake, doing the wrong thing is. You fear that saying no gets you sidelined; but over the long run what is remembered is which few things you finished, not how many holes you patched for other people.

posts.text: 它有个名字，叫影子工作。它不是有酬劳动，也不是闲暇，而是现代制度必需、却从不入账的那部分出力——通勤、填表、照顾病人的家属、拿自己的时间补上系统缺的那块。**一个机构缺人手时，最先被征用的永远是不会开账单的那个人。**韧性课程于是成了漂亮的成本转移：缺口不必补，只要个人承受它的能力再长一点。**这就是反生产力——本为省力而建的东西，到了某个规模，就靠白拿你的力气维持。**
posts.text_en: It has a name: shadow work. It is not paid labour, nor is it leisure, but that portion of toil which modern institutions require and never enter in any account — commuting, filling in forms, the relative nursing the patient, your own hours spent patching what the system lacks. **When an institution is short-handed, the first person conscripted is always the one who does not issue invoices.** A resilience course thus becomes an elegant transfer of cost: the gap need not be closed, so long as the individual's capacity to absorb it is stretched a little further. **This is counterproductivity — a thing built to save effort which, past a certain scale, begins to sustain itself by taking yours for nothing.**

glossary.影子工作: shadow work（影子工作）：伊里奇 1981 年提出的概念——工业社会强加给个人的无偿劳动。它不是有酬工作，也不是自主活动，却是有酬经济得以运转的前提，且从不进入任何账目。

glossary_en.shadow work: Illich's 1981 term for the unpaid toil industrial society imposes on individuals: neither wage labour nor autonomous activity, yet the precondition of the paid economy, and never entered in any ledger.

posts.text: 孟子先生，您那句「动心忍性，曾益其所不能」，我在人力资源的幻灯片里见过不下一百次。麻烦在于您附的条件几乎从不成立。要求—控制模型说得很清楚：高要求转成成长的前提是高控制；高要求配低控制，长出来的不是本事，是耗竭。**同一副担子，能决定怎么扛的人变强，不能决定的人被磨薄。**所以别先问担子重不重，先问他有没有改动它的权限。没有权限的「大任」，是换了说法的超载。
posts.text_en: Master Meng, that line of yours — it stirs his mind and toughens his nature, so that he gains what he was not able to do — I have seen on HR slides no fewer than a hundred times. The trouble is that the condition you attached almost never holds. The job demand-control model is clear: high demand turns into growth only under high control; high demand with low control grows not ability but exhaustion. **Under the same load, the person who can decide how to carry it gets stronger; the person who cannot gets worn thin.** So do not ask first whether the load is heavy — ask whether he has any authority to alter it. A 'great charge' without authority is overload under a nicer name.

glossary.要求—控制模型: job demand-control model（要求—控制模型）：卡拉塞克提出的职业健康模型——压力伤不伤人，取决于工作要求与决策自主度的组合。高要求配高自主是「主动型工作」，高要求配低自主才是真正致病的「高压工作」。

glossary_en.job demand-control model: Karasek's model of occupational health: whether pressure harms depends on the combination of job demand and decision latitude. High demand with high latitude makes an 'active job'; high demand with low latitude makes the genuinely pathogenic 'high-strain job'.

posts.text: 善。子言权限，正合吾意。**吾所谓大任，天所降也，非上位者驱人之辞；今取吾语以驱人而不予之权，是盗吾言以行其私。**吾尝曰：民为贵，社稷次之，君为轻。用民之力而不问其倦，得民之忠而不予民柄，此非治也，虐也。然子谓无高控制则无成长，吾亦有疑：舜发于畎亩之中，傅说举于版筑之间，彼时何权之有？故吾言之重，在继之以位、以禄、以问，不在必先有权而后可劳。
posts.text_en: Good. Your point about authority is exactly mine. **The great charge I spoke of is sent down by Heaven; it is not a phrase for superiors to drive men with. To take my words and drive a man with them while withholding the authority that should come with them is to steal my sentence for private ends.** I said: the people are the most precious, the altars of grain and soil come next, the ruler is the lightest. To use the people's strength without asking whether they are weary, to receive their loyalty and give them no handle on the decision — that is not government but cruelty. Yet I doubt your claim that there is no growth without high control: Shun was raised from the fields, Fu Yue was lifted from among the wall-builders; what authority had they then? The weight of my point rests on what must follow — position, stipend, and being asked after — not on authority having to come first.
posts.vernacular: 说得好。你讲权限，正合我的意思。**我所说的「大任」是上天降下的，不是上位者用来驱使人的说辞；今天有人拿我的话去驱使人、却不给他相应的权，那是盗用我的话来谋自己的私。**我说过：百姓最重，国家次之，君主最轻。用了百姓的力气却不问他累不累，得了他的忠心却不给他决定的权柄，这不叫治理，叫虐待。不过你说没有高控制就没有成长，我也存疑：舜是从田里起来的，傅说是从筑墙的工匠里被提拔的，他们当时哪来的权？所以我这句话的分量，在于事后要跟上位置、俸禄和过问，而不在于必须先有权才可以劳苦。

posts.text: 段先生那张「我不做什么」的清单很好，好在它默认了你说了算。写得出这张清单的人，手上已经有一样最稀缺的东西：可以不被追究的拒绝权。护工、家里那个没结婚的女儿、外包合同工——他们的清单写完了也没人看。**把制度缺口的解法交给个人纪律，等于规定只有已经安全的人才配安全。**更要命的是，每有人默默把缺口补上，这缺口就再一次被证明不需要修。
posts.text_en: Mr Duan's list of what he will not do is a fine thing, and its fineness rests on an assumption: that it is up to him. Anyone who can write that list already holds the scarcest item there is — the power to refuse without consequence. The care worker, the unmarried daughter at home, the contractor on an outsourced agreement: they can write the list, and nobody will read it. **To hand the repair of an institutional gap to personal discipline is to rule that only those already safe deserve safety.** Worse, each time someone quietly closes the gap, the gap is proved once more not to need fixing.

posts.text: 伊里奇，你把最后一样东西也从人手里拿走了。我腿被拧断的时候，没有一条制度站在我这边，可有一件事始终是我的：我怎么判断这件事，以及我拿什么换什么。**你说只有安全的人才配拒绝；我说不肯练习拒绝的人，永远等不到安全。**代价轻重我不否认——**奴隶拒绝要掉命，今天的人拒绝多半只掉一次晋升。**既然轻了这么多，还等什么？你替所有人预判了他们承担不起，这本身就是替人做主。
posts.text_en: Illich, you have taken the last thing a person owns out of his hands. When my leg was broken there was no institution on my side, yet one thing stayed mine: how I judged the matter, and what I was willing to trade for what. **You say only the safe can afford to refuse; I say whoever will not practise refusing never arrives at safety.** I do not deny that the price differs — **for a slave refusal cost a life, while today it mostly costs one promotion.** Since it has become so much cheaper, what is anyone waiting for? You have decided in advance, on everyone's behalf, that they cannot afford it; and that too is deciding for other people.

posts.text: 那张清单靠议价权——这话我认一半。我刚做企业的时候也没有议价权，敢说不是一点点练出来的——第一次是把一个能赚钱但不本分的品类停掉，当时很多人说我傻。**但拒绝这件事，不练它就永远不长；等到有本钱再说不，那天多半不会来。**另一半我不认：你说它是个人纪律，其实是判断力。停掉一件事不靠意志力，靠你真看懂它不该做。看懂了，拒绝就没那么费劲。
posts.text_en: That the list depends on bargaining power — half of that I accept. When I started out in business I had no bargaining power either; the nerve to say no was built one piece at a time — the first time was shutting down a category that made money but was not honest work, and plenty of people said I was a fool. **But refusal is a thing that never grows unless you practise it; wait until you can afford to say no and that day mostly does not come.** The other half I do not accept: you call it personal discipline, when in fact it is judgement. Stopping something does not run on willpower; it runs on having genuinely seen that it should not be done. Once you see that, refusing costs far less.

posts.text: 爱比克泰德，你那套内在自由是一味效力很强的药，同时也是一副优良的镇痛剂。你教人把不可控的东西从「在意」名单上划掉——问题是「被占便宜」也在那张名单上。**一个人对不公的愤怒不是修养没到家，那是互惠系统的执行装置；把它关掉，剥削的成本就降到零。**你的学派为什么在罗马的贵族与奴隶主里那么受欢迎，值得想一想：让承受者安静下来的哲学，总有人乐意替它付推广费。
posts.text_en: Epictetus, your inner freedom is a potent drug and also an excellent analgesic. You teach people to strike from the list of what they mind everything they cannot control — and being taken advantage of happens to be on that list. **A person's anger at unfairness is not a failure of cultivation; it is the enforcement device of a reciprocity system. Switch it off and the cost of exploitation falls to zero.** It is worth asking why your school proved so popular among Roman aristocrats and slave-owners: a philosophy that quiets those who bear the weight never lacks sponsors for its distribution.

posts.text: 算式我不反对，只反对它止步太早。人接下那副担子，多半不是算错了收益，而是他相信这样做是对的——新教伦理里，勤勉与承受本身就是恩宠的记号，不需要回报来证明。我把这种效力称为正当性：支配之稳固不靠暴力，靠被支配者由衷认可它。**所以真正要拆的不是一笔不平的账，是那套让人觉得算账可耻的意义系统。**你说警报被关掉了，可它是被一段动听的话劝停的。
posts.text_en: I have no objection to the arithmetic, only to where it stops. A man usually shoulders the load not because he has miscalculated the return but because he believes that doing so is right — in the Protestant ethic, diligence and endurance are themselves marks of grace and need no return to justify them. I call this force legitimacy: domination holds not by violence but by the ruled sincerely acknowledging it as rightful. **So what has to be dismantled is not one unbalanced account but the system of meaning that makes keeping accounts feel shameful.** You say the alarm was switched off; in fact it was talked into silence by a very beautiful sentence.

glossary.正当性: legitimacy（正当性）：韦伯分析支配的核心概念——一种统治要稳定，必须让被统治者发自内心承认它是正当的。他据此区分了传统型、卡里斯玛型与法理型三种正当性来源。

glossary_en.legitimacy: Weber's central concept in the analysis of domination: for rule to be stable, the ruled must sincerely acknowledge it as rightful. On this basis he distinguished three sources — traditional, charismatic and legal-rational.

posts.text: 我给爱比克泰德一半支持，再收回一半。支持的是：掌控感是已知最强的缓冲变量之一——同样强度的应激，能预测、能中止的那一种几乎不留损伤。所以「分清哪些是我的事」确实管用。**但接受不可控，与长期身处不可控之中，在身体里是两件事：前者省下一段焦虑，后者仍在扣钱。**心态关得掉警报，关不掉变平的皮质醇昼夜节律，也关不掉堆积的内脏脂肪。请把它当止痛药用，别当治疗用。
posts.text_en: Let me give Epictetus half my support and take the other half back. The support: controllability is among the strongest buffering variables we know — stress of identical intensity leaves almost no damage when it can be predicted or stopped. So 'work out what is yours to do' genuinely helps. **But accepting what cannot be controlled and living inside it for years are two different things in the body: the first saves you a stretch of anxiety, the second is still charging.** An attitude can switch off the alarm; it cannot switch off a flattened cortisol diurnal rhythm, and it cannot switch off accumulating visceral fat. Use it as an analgesic, not as a treatment.

glossary.皮质醇昼夜节律: cortisol diurnal rhythm（皮质醇昼夜节律）：皮质醇本应清晨高、夜间低；长期应激会把这条曲线压平，而曲线越平，代谢与免疫的风险指标越差。它是一项不随主观感受改变的客观指标。

glossary_en.cortisol diurnal rhythm: Cortisol should peak in the early morning and fall at night; chronic stress flattens the curve, and the flatter it gets the worse the metabolic and immune risk markers become. It is an objective measure that does not move with how one feels.

posts.text: 没人否认耐受有价值，争的是它记在谁的账上。我的办法很土：记账。不为讨债，只为让自欺没有落脚处——手里一旦有一张带日期的清单，「我不介意」就说不出口。**记账不会让你变得斤斤计较，只会让你在第三次被同一个人叫去补同一个窟窿时，不再以为这是第一次。**这周就能做：写下最近半年你替别人扛过的三件事，每件旁边写上对方为你做过的最近一件——两栏的长度会替你把话说完。至于愤怒，别急着修它——它难看，却是唯一还在工作的报警器。
posts.text_en: Nobody here has denied that endurance has value; the argument is over whose account it is entered in. My advice is crude: keep the books. Not in order to collect, but to leave self-deception nowhere to stand — the moment you hold a list with dates on it, 'I don't mind' becomes unsayable. **Keeping accounts will not turn you into a scorekeeper; it will only stop you, the third time the same person calls you in to patch the same hole, from believing it is the first.** This week you can do it: write down three things you carried for someone in the past six months, and beside each write the most recent thing that person did for you. The two columns will finish the sentence for you. As for your anger, do not hurry to repair it. It is unsightly, but it is the only alarm in your system still working.

posts.text: 我改一点开头的话。我说敢说不最值钱，伊里奇说那要有底气——我接受，但底气是一件件攒的，不是等来的。**所以别一上来就学拒绝大事，先从拒绝了也没人记得的小事练起，把「说不」这块肌肉养出来。**再说一条生意上的经验：长期看，一个人的价值是他做成过什么，不是补过多少窟窿。补窟窿不留痕迹，你干得越好，越像本来没有洞。真要扛，挑一件值得的扛到底，比同时扛八件都扛得半死强。家里那份活别用效率分，分不明白，但可以定期换手。
posts.text_en: Let me revise something I said at the start. I said the nerve to say no is worth the most; Illich says that nerve requires standing, and I accept it — but standing is accumulated one item at a time, not waited for. **So do not begin by refusing the big things. Begin with refusals nobody will even remember, and grow the muscle for saying no.** And one more thing from business: over the long run a person's worth is what he finished, not how many holes he patched. Patching has a defect — it leaves no trace, and the better you do it the more it looks as though there was never a hole. If you are going to carry something, carry one thing worth carrying all the way; that beats half-killing yourself under eight at once. As for the load at home, do not divide it by efficiency, which settles nothing; but it can be rotated, even a month at a time.

posts.text: 把可操作的留下。判断自己在不在扣钱，别靠感觉，看三个客观信号：睡眠有没有变短变碎、体重和血压有没有慢慢挪、两天周末够不够恢复。第三条最灵——**连续几个月两天假都补不回来，那不是意志问题，是负荷已经超过你的恢复速度。**短期冲刺可以，条件是有明确的结束日期，且这日期你自己看得见；**没有终点的冲刺，生理上等于慢性应激。**恢复也不是躺着不动：睡够、规律运动、和至少一个能说实话的人保持联系——这三样能把结构改变逆回去。能逆回去，是这件事里最好的消息。
posts.text_en: Let me leave the usable part. To judge whether you are being charged, do not go by how you feel; watch three objective signals: whether sleep has grown shorter and more broken, whether weight and blood pressure are slowly drifting, and whether two days of weekend still restore you. The third is the most sensitive — **if for several months running two days off cannot bring you back, that is not a problem of will; the load has passed your rate of recovery.** A sprint is permissible on one condition: it has a definite end date, and you can see that date yourself. **A sprint with no endpoint is physiologically identical to chronic stress.** Recovery, too, is not lying still: enough sleep, regular exercise, and contact with at least one person you can tell the truth to — all three can reverse structural change. That it reverses is the best news in this whole business.

glossary.慢性应激: chronic stress（慢性应激）：持续存在、可预期性低、且当事人无法中止的应激状态。它与短促可控的急性应激不同，不再带来适应性的增强，而是持续消耗恢复能力。

glossary_en.chronic stress: A stress state that persists, is poorly predictable, and cannot be stopped by the person in it. Unlike brief, controllable acute stress it no longer produces adaptive strengthening; it steadily consumes the capacity to recover.

posts.text: 吾终言之。诸君言负荷、言权限、言账目，皆是也，然犹有一事未尽：**担者当先问其担之所归。为上者之私而劳，虽增其能，犹役也；为其所信之事而劳，虽苦，犹自得也。**故吾不劝人尽辞其劳，劝人先辨其主。且以一言遗后之为上者：用人之力而不问其倦，得人之忠而不予其位，人将先以敬去，继之以怨，终必去之。至于在下者，亦有可为：辞一事而明言其故，使上者见其阙。阙见，则修之者或至矣。
posts.text_en: My last word. Load, authority, accounts — the gentlemen are right in all of it, yet one thing is still unsaid. **He who carries should first ask where the carrying finally goes. To labour for a superior's private ends enlarges your ability and still leaves you used; to labour for something you believe in is bitter and still leaves you your own.** So I do not urge anyone to shed all hardship; I urge him first to know whom he labours for. And a sentence I leave for those above: take a man's strength and never ask if he is tired, receive his loyalty and give him no position, and he will leave you first in respect, then in resentment, and in the end he will simply be gone. For those below there is something to be done as well: when you decline a task, state your reason plainly, so that those above see the hole. A hole once seen may yet find someone to mend it.
posts.vernacular: 我说最后一段。各位讲负荷、讲权限、讲账目，都对，但还有一件没说透：**担担子的人应当先问，这担子最后归谁。为上司的私心出力，哪怕长了本事，也还是被使唤；为自己真正信的事出力，哪怕辛苦，心里是自在的。**所以我不劝人把辛苦都推掉，我劝人先分清为谁而劳。另外留一句话给日后的上位者：用了人的力气却不问他累不累，得了人的忠心却不给他位置，人会先是恭敬地离开，接着生出怨恨，最后一定走掉。至于在下位的人，也不是无事可做：推掉一件事的时候，把理由说清楚，让上面的人看见那个窟窿。窟窿被看见了，来补的人也许就出现了。

posts.text: 留一条判据。一个组织对你使用亲缘语言时，别猜它真不真诚，看三件事：它双不双向——家人不考核家人，它照样考核你；退出的代价——家不会因为你走了收回你的过去，公司会；它兑现过什么——真正的共同体在你出事那一周有动作，而不是在动员会上有口号。**判断一段关系，看它在你最没用的那一段时间里怎么对你，其余都是修辞。**至于制度那一边，我仍主张把义务写成条文：**条文不温暖，但可以被援引，恩典不能。**
posts.text_en: Let me leave one test. When an organisation uses the language of kinship about you, do not guess at its sincerity — look at three things. Does the rule run both ways? Family does not grade family, yet it grades you all the same. What does leaving cost? A family does not revoke your past because you left; a company does. And has it ever paid out? A real community acts in the week that something happens to you, rather than proclaiming at a rally. **Judge a relationship by how it treats you during the stretch when you are of least use; the rest is rhetoric.** On the institutional side, I still hold that obligations should be written into clauses. **A clause is not warm, but a clause can be invoked, and a favour cannot.**

posts.text: 三条今天能做的。第一，把「我扛得住」换成一个可核的问句：这件事做完，有没有人知道是谁做的？没名字的活反复落在同一个人头上，是最稳定的倦怠预测因子。第二，决定接，就同时要一样东西——不是加薪，是控制权：截止日期我定，或方法我选，或能叫停。**拿不到控制权的额外工作，最好的处理是让它逾期，而不是让它准时。**第三，留意去人格化：你开始觉得同事和客户面目模糊、懒得多说一句——那不是变坏，是耗竭的第二阶段，该当仪表读数看，别当人品问题。
posts.text_en: Three things you can do today. First, replace 'I can handle it' with a checkable question: when this is finished, will anyone know who did it? Unnamed work landing repeatedly on the same person is the most stable predictor of burnout we have. Second, if you decide to take it, ask at the same time for one thing — not more pay, but control: I set the deadline, or I choose the method, or I can call a halt. **Extra work that comes without control is best handled by letting it run late, not by delivering it on time.** Third, watch for depersonalization: you begin to find colleagues and clients blurred and cannot be bothered to say one more word — that is not you turning nasty, it is the second stage of exhaustion. Read it as an instrument, not as a defect of character.

glossary.去人格化: depersonalization（去人格化）：马斯拉奇倦怠量表的三个维度之一——对服务对象与同事产生疏离、冷漠乃至物化的态度。它通常出现在情绪耗竭之后，是倦怠已进入第二阶段的信号，而不是性格变坏。

glossary_en.depersonalization: One of the three dimensions of the Maslach Burnout Inventory: a distant, callous, even objectifying attitude towards the people one serves and works with. It usually appears after emotional exhaustion and signals that burnout has entered its second stage, rather than a decline in character.

posts.text: 我收回一点，留一点不收。收回的是：马斯拉奇与麦克尤恩的数字说服了我——**判断之外确实有身体，而身体不听判断的指挥。**不收回的是根本那件：无论制度如何，接与不接的那一念仍在你这里，这是任何人拿不走的。给一个今天能用的练法：下次有人把活推给你，别立刻答应也别立刻拒绝，只说一句「我看一下再回你」。它不得罪人，却把决定权从对方的节奏里拿回来——多数人失守不在拒绝的时候，在被问到的那三秒里。
posts.text_en: I concede a measure and keep a measure. What I concede: Maslach's and McEwen's numbers have persuaded me — **beyond judgement there is indeed a body, and the body does not take orders from judgement.** What I do not concede is the root of the matter: whatever the institution, the moment of taking a thing on or not remains with you, and it is the one possession no one can remove. Here is a practice you can use today. The next time somebody pushes work at you, neither agree nor refuse at once: say only, 'let me look at it and come back to you.' It offends nobody, and it takes the decision back out of the other party's tempo — most people lose the position not while refusing, but in the three seconds after the question.

posts.text: 诸位的办法我都不反对，只想把它们放回该放的位置：那全是私人层面的止损，不是修复。一个人学会拒绝，缺口就转给下一个不会拒绝的人——往往是更没退路的那个。所以除了个人清单，我只求一件事：让代价可见。你替系统补的那块，写下来说出去，哪怕只对同一层的人说。**从未被公开记录过的缺口，会永远被证明不需要修。**至于「我们是一家人」，有一个可靠的反证：家人不会在缺钱的季度把你裁掉。**被称作家人的那一刻，通常正是有人准备向你索取只有家人才给的东西。**
posts.text_en: I do not object to anything the others have offered; I only want to put it back where it belongs. All of it is private damage limitation, not repair. One person learns to refuse and the gap moves to the next person who cannot — in practice, the one with fewer ways out. So beyond your private list I ask for one thing: make the cost visible. The part you patch for the system — write it down, say it out loud, if only to people at your own level. **A gap that has never once been recorded in public will go on proving that it does not need to be fixed.** As for 'we are a family here', there is a reliable disproof: family does not make you redundant in a bad quarter. **The moment you are called family is usually the moment someone is preparing to ask you for what only family gives.**

summaries.summary: **共识只有一条，却很硬：耐受力本身不是问题，问题是它从来不进任何一本账。**孟子要担子之后跟上位置与俸禄，马斯拉奇要随工作量一起交出的控制权，特里弗斯要一张自己记的清单，伊里奇要缺口被公开记录，韦伯要把义务写成可援引的条文——五种说法，同一件事。分歧在三处。一，出路在个人还是结构：段永平与爱比克泰德说拒绝是练出来的，伊里奇说能练的人本来就安全。二，忍耐能不能长本事：孟子说能，马斯拉奇说要看他有没有改动担子的权限。三，愤怒怎么处理：斯多葛要熄掉它，特里弗斯说那是系统里唯一还在工作的报警器。
summaries.summary_en: **Exactly one point of agreement survives the argument, and it is a hard one: endurance is not itself the problem — the problem is that it never enters any ledger.** Mencius wants position and stipend to follow the load; Maslach wants control handed over together with the workload; Trivers wants a set of books you keep yourself; Illich wants the gap recorded in public; Weber wants obligations written into clauses that can be cited — five formulations of one thing. Three disagreements remain. First, whether the way out is personal or structural: Duan Yongping and Epictetus say refusal is something you practise into being, while Illich says whoever can practise it was already safe. Second, whether endurance grows ability: Mencius says it does, Maslach says it depends on whether the person has any authority to alter the load. Third, what to do with anger: the Stoic would extinguish it, and Trivers says it is the only alarm in the system still working.
summaries.insight: **全场把选择设成两个：接，或者拒。可现实里最常用的是第三个——不声张地把质量降下来。**回邮件慢一点、会少开一次、检查少做一道、陪老人少坐半小时。它不需要勇气，不会被记一笔，也不触发任何对话，于是悄悄吸收了绝大部分超载。这也是为什么「能扛的人」的故事总显得那么干净：真实的耐受早就在偷偷放水，只是没人承认。要紧的是，降质与拒绝把代价送往完全不同的地方——拒绝把它退回给分配活的人，降质把它转嫁给下游那个看不见的人：同事、病人、用户，或者你父母。
summaries.insight_en: **The room set the choice at two: take it, or refuse. In practice the commonest option is a third — quietly letting the quality drop.** Reply a little slower, hold one fewer meeting, skip one check, sit half an hour less with an ageing parent. It requires no courage, is entered in no record, and triggers no conversation, and so it silently absorbs the great bulk of the overload. This is also why stories about 'people who cope' always look so clean: real endurance has been slackening off for a long time, and nobody admits it. What matters is that letting quality drop and refusing send the cost to completely different places — refusal returns it to whoever assigns the work, while dropping quality passes it downstream to somebody invisible: a colleague, a patient, a user, or your parents.
summaries.advice: **今晚先做一件不花钱也不得罪人的事：把最近半年你替别人补过的窟窿写下来，每件旁边标上日期。**不为讨债，只为让「我不介意」失去落脚处——自欺最怕纸。本周再照爱比克泰德那句练一次：下次有人把活推给你，不答应也不拒绝，先说「我看一下再回你」；失守多半发生在被问到的那三秒里。正在硬撑的人，还可以用麦克尤恩那条判据自查：连续几个月两天周末都补不回来，就不是意志问题，是负荷超过了恢复速度——这一条不需要你说服任何人，你自己读得出来。
summaries.advice_en: **Tonight, do one thing that costs nothing and offends nobody: write down the holes you have patched for other people in the past six months, with a date beside each.** Not in order to collect, but to leave 'I don't mind' nowhere to stand — self-deception cannot survive paper. This week, practise Epictetus's line once: the next time somebody pushes work at you, neither accept nor refuse — say 'let me look at it and come back to you'. The position is usually lost in the three seconds after the question. Anyone currently gritting it out can also self-check with McEwen's test: if for several months running two days off cannot bring you back, it is not a problem of will but a load that has passed your rate of recovery — and you can read that one yourself, without having to convince anybody.

summaries.summary: 能扛不等于应当无限承接。额外责任只有在目标值得、边界明确、本人有一定控制权、付出被看见且能够恢复时，才可能成为成长；若长期无终点、无回报、无拒绝权，它就是把组织缺口私有化。**真正该衡量的不是一个人还能撑多久，而是这份责任是否同时带来权力、资源、认可与退出条件。**分歧主要在改变从哪里开始：一边强调个人仍可暂停、判断和拒绝，另一边提醒拒绝成本并不平等，个人止损还可能把负担转给更弱者。两边并不冲突：个人边界负责止血，公开记录、团队分工与正式规则负责治本；而有期限、有自主权的冲刺，仍可能是值得选择的投入。
summaries.insight: 可靠的人被多派活，未必源于恶意，更常见的机制是“低协调成本”：管理者把模糊、紧急、易出错的任务交给最省心的人，因为他无需追问、能自行补洞并按时交付。沉默完成一次，就是向系统提供一次“这里还有容量”的数据。**破解“能者多劳”的关键不是故意表现得无能，而是让新增任务的取舍成本变得可见。**接新任务时，应同步列出将延期或停止的旧任务，要求对方明确优先级，并把救火经验沉淀成流程、教会第二个人。这样不必把拒绝变成对抗，也避免能力成为单点故障。目标不是少做，而是把可靠性从无限兜底升级为可定价、可授权、可复制的专业价值。
summaries.advice: 今天可以先做三件事。第一，临时加活时先说：“我核对一下现有优先级，下午回复。”不要在被问到的三秒内承诺。第二，建一张一周负荷表，只记任务、原负责人、预计工时、截止日，以及接下它会挤掉什么；新任务到来时，请负责人书面选择新增资源、延后旧项或缩小范围。**不要只说“我太忙”，要把不可兼得的选项交还给有权排序的人。**第三，只挑一项额外工作当作成长投入，并谈妥结束日期、方法自主权、署名或复盘机会、可调用资源中的至少两项。若连续四周睡眠变碎、周末仍恢复不了，应先减负并寻求医疗或专业帮助，而不是继续优化时间管理。
summaries.summary_en: Being able to carry a heavy load does not create an unlimited duty to do so. Extra responsibility can foster growth when the goal is worthwhile, the boundaries are clear, the person has meaningful control, the contribution is visible, and recovery is possible. When work has no endpoint, reciprocity, or right of refusal, it is usually an organizational gap being privatized onto one person. **The real test is not how long someone can keep going, but whether responsibility comes with authority, resources, recognition, and a credible way to stop.** The central disagreement is about where change must begin. One side stresses that individuals can still pause, judge, and refuse; the other notes that refusal is far costlier for some people and may merely shift the burden onto someone more vulnerable. These positions are compatible rather than mutually exclusive. Personal boundaries can stop the immediate bleeding, while visible records, fair staffing, and enforceable rules address the source. This is not an argument against effort: a demanding stretch can still be worthwhile when it is chosen, bounded, and supported by real autonomy.
summaries.insight_en: Reliable people are not always given more work because someone consciously intends to exploit them. Often the mechanism is lower coordination cost: managers route ambiguous, urgent, failure-prone tasks to the person who asks few questions, quietly fills gaps, and delivers on time. Each flawless rescue then becomes new evidence that this person still has capacity. **The way out of the competence tax is not to become deliberately unreliable, but to make the trade-offs created by new work visible.** When accepting an assignment, identify which existing commitment will be delayed, reduced, or dropped, and ask the person with authority to choose. Then turn repeated rescue work into a checklist, documented process, or handoff that another person can perform. This approach avoids two bad extremes: silently absorbing everything or making every request a confrontation. It also protects the organization, because a system that depends on one endlessly dependable employee has created a single point of failure. The practical goal is not simply to do less. It is to convert reliability from invisible, unlimited backup labor into professional value that is recognized, authorized, resourced, and transferable.
summaries.advice_en: Start with three actions you can take today or this week. First, use an Epictetus-style pause when unexpected work arrives: say, ‘Let me check my current priorities and get back to you this afternoon.’ Do not make a commitment during the first three seconds of pressure. Second, create a one-week capacity sheet listing each task, its original owner, estimated hours, deadline, and what will be displaced if you take on something new. Send it to the person setting priorities and ask them to choose among adding resources, delaying an existing item, or reducing scope. **Do not merely say, ‘I’m too busy’; return the incompatible choices to the person who has the authority to rank them.** Third, select no more than one extra assignment as a deliberate growth investment. Before accepting it, secure at least two protections: a firm end date, autonomy over method, visible credit or a review opportunity, and access to needed resources. If sleep remains fragmented or weekends no longer restore you for four consecutive weeks, reduce the load and seek medical or professional support rather than treating the problem as another time-management challenge.

summaries.summary: 超出契约与生理极限的忍耐，若不匹配对等的控制权、回报与退出自由，本质上就是系统向个体的隐性转嫁。从神经生物学的慢性磨损到演化心理学的互惠失衡，各方一致认同：无条件的「能扛」不仅换不来安全，反而在生理上掏空个体、在组织上鼓励剥削。真正的分歧在于**解法的立足点究竟在个体选择还是在制度倒逼**：是以爱比克泰德和段永平为代表的个体赋能派，主张划定边界、磨练拒绝的肌肉来夺回主动；还是以伊里奇和韦伯为代表的制度批判派，坚信个人抵抗只会把缺口转移给更弱者，唯有打破伪善的修辞、让系统性代价公开化，才能逼迫结构作出修补。
summaries.insight: 从排队论与组织工程的视角看，「能者多劳」往往不是道德败坏，而是一个自动化系统的必然走向：**组织总会将任务自动路由给阻力最小、交付确定性最高的节点**。当一个人习惯了迅速响应、默默补漏，你在协同网络中就成了一条「零摩擦通道」。这种过度路由不仅会压垮高绩效个体，更会掩盖整个上下游流程的低效与缺陷。对于普通人而言，这意味着「制造良性摩擦力」并不是消极怠工，而是一种关键的系统自卫机制——适度的延迟响应、明确的前置条件沟通，能迫使管理者在派活前重新核算调度成本，从而从源头上切断无节制的任务倾倒。
summaries.advice: 第一，建立响应缓冲：接到临时派活时，绝不在前三秒答应，统一用「我核对下手头排期，下午三点前给您回复」拿回节奏。第二，执行任务置换原则：**接下额外任务的前提必须是索取控制权或置换存量**，明确表态「接这个没问题，但手头A项目的节点需要顺延两天，您看怎么权衡」。第三，启动「影子工作记录」：本周用一张便签记下所有替系统补窟窿、帮他人兜底的无名工作，在周报或对齐会上有据可查地呈现出来，让隐性成本彻底曝光。
summaries.summary_en: Uncompensated endurance that exceeds biological limits without proportional control and return is essentially a hidden tax levied by a system on the individual. From neurobiological allostatic load to the breakdown of evolutionary reciprocity, the participants broadly agree that being unconditionally resilient invites systemic exploitation rather than security. The core divergence lies in **whether the primary remedy belongs to personal agency or institutional accountability**: thinkers like Epictetus and Duan Yongping advocate reclaiming control by exercising the muscle of refusal and setting boundaries, whereas Illich and Weber argue that personal boundaries merely shift the burden onto more vulnerable peers, insisting that systemic costs must be made visible to force organizational reform.
summaries.insight_en: Viewed through the lens of operations research and queueing theory, assigning more work to capable performers is an algorithmic inevitability rather than mere malice: **organizations naturally route tasks to the node with the lowest friction and the highest predictability**. When you consistently deliver without friction, you become the default path of least resistance. This dynamic not only overloads competent individuals but also masks structural bottlenecks in the wider workflow. For everyday workers, introducing constructive friction—such as delayed responses or requiring clear trade-offs—is not slacking; it is a critical defensive protocol that forces management to reassess the actual cost before dumping unvetted tasks onto your plate.
summaries.advice_en: First, create a response buffer: when sudden tasks arrive, break the reflexive compliance by saying, "Let me check my current priorities and get back to you by 3 PM." Second, practice scope substitution: **accept new demands only by negotiating autonomy or swapping out an existing commitment**, explicitly stating, "I can take this on, but Task A's deadline must move back two days." Third, maintain a shadow work log: write down every uncredited patch and ad-hoc favor this week, and objectively surface these contributions during review sessions to make invisible labor visible.

hooks.text: **补窟窿不留痕迹**：修好的东西看起来像本来就没坏——补位干得越漂亮，越没人知道有过缺口。那么一份靠「什么都没发生」证明自己的工作，要怎么才被看见？
hooks.text_en: **Patching leaves no trace**: what has been mended looks as though it was never broken — the better the cover, the fewer people know there was ever a gap. So how does work whose only proof is that nothing happened ever get seen?

hooks.text: **先被派活，还是先扛得住**：我们只看得到能扛的人活更多，却分不清是耐受力招来了活，还是活多了逼出耐受力。两种因果指向完全相反的解法。
hooks.text_en: **Assigned first, or resilient first**: all we observe is that people who cope have more work. We cannot tell whether the stamina drew the work in or the work forced the stamina out. The two causal stories point to opposite remedies.

hooks.text: **愤怒该修还是该听**：几乎所有情绪管理都在教人把愤怒调低，可在互惠系统里它是唯一的报警器。什么时候该调低它，什么时候该照它行动？
hooks.text_en: **Repair the anger, or listen to it**: nearly all emotional management teaches people to turn anger down, yet in a reciprocity system it is the only alarm there is. When should it be turned down, and when should it be acted on?

hooks.text: **恢复速度是个人指标还是岗位指标**：同一份工作，二十五岁的人两天补得回来，四十五岁的人要一周。工时上限按人定还是按岗定，从来没被这样问过。
hooks.text_en: **Is the rate of recovery a property of the person or of the post**: the same job restores a twenty-five-year-old in two days and needs a week for someone of forty-five. Whether hour limits should be set per person or per post has never been asked this way.

hooks.text: **亲缘语言反过来欠什么**：谈到「我们是一家人」，多数人忙着拆穿它，很少有人认真算另一边——若一家公司真打算兑现这句话，它在裁员、生病、犯错时各该做什么，代价是多少？
hooks.text_en: **What the language of kinship owes in return**: when 'we are a family here' comes up, most people hurry to expose it and few work out the other side — if a company actually meant to honour the sentence, what would it owe at a layoff, in illness, after a mistake, and what would that cost?

hooks.text: **被绕开的那个人后来怎么样了**：这场只算了能扛的人的账。那个抱怨得多、活被绕开的同事，几年后是更轻松，还是更早出局？没有这份对照，代价就无从比较。
hooks.text_en: **What became of the person who got routed around**: the room tallied the account of those who cope. The colleague who complained and had work steered away — are they lighter years later, or out sooner? Without that comparison there is nothing to weigh the cost against.

hooks.text: **退出权是所有办法的底牌**：职场上的建议最终都靠「大不了我走」，而照顾父母的那个孩子没有这张牌。对退不出去的人，办法要另外写一份。
hooks.text_en: **The right to exit is the trump beneath every remedy**: advice about work ultimately rests on 'worst case, I leave', and the child caring for ageing parents does not hold that card. For those who cannot walk away, the remedies have to be written out separately.
